newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CANTV details lines modernization plans.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CANTV details lines modernization plans.

text.p: Venezuelan telephone company CANTV said it plans to install more than 200,000 digital lines in 1997 as part of its network modernization.
It said in a statement that 277,600 digital lines were installed this year for a total of 3.21 million installed lines throughout the country, up from 1.99 million five years ago.

In a presentation of its strategy for the rest of the decade, CANTV said it would operate a high capacity fiber optic network in 1999 and 900,000 additional lines for the year 2000 when CANTV's monopoly expires.

CANTV Vice President for Communications and External Relations Alvaro Benavides said the company had boosted the number of lines per 100 inhabitants from 7.5 to 11.5 since a consortium led by GTE Corp bought a 40 percent stake in the company in 1991.
By the year 2000, that ratio should be 13.3, putting Venezuela in a very competitive position in Latin America, he told a Foreign Press Club meeting Thursday night.
Benavides said CANTV's development plans were based on the assumption that an IMF-inspired economic reform program launched in April would bear fruit in years to come.
The Venezuelan government raised nearly $900 million last month through the sale of most of its 49 percent stake in CANTV.

Benavides also said CANTV would focus investments on other telephone services such as the construction of 2,200 community telecommunications centers by the year 2000. Set in low-income areas, these centers allow residents access to pay phones and fax and message services.
"This is CANTV reaching out to all Venezuelans," he said.
